speaker: Sheldon
text: Here's the problem with teleportation. Assuming a device could be invented which would identify the quantum state of matter of an individual in one location and transmit that pattern to a distant location for reassembly, you would not have actually transported the individual. You would have destroyed him in one location and recreated him in another.

speaker: Leonard
text: Lay it on me. How about that?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Personally, I would never use a transporter because the original Sheldon would have to be disintegrated in order to create a new Sheldon.

speaker: Leonard
text: Would the new Sheldon be in any way an improvement on the old Sheldon?

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, he would be exactly the same.

speaker: Leonard
text: That is a problem.

speaker: Sheldon
text: So you see it too.

speaker: Leonard
text: Doctor Hofstadter Cooper Cable hoser Gentlemen, I'd like you to meet Dennis Kim. Dennis is a highly sought-after doctoral candidate. We're hoping to have him do his graduate work here.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Graduate work.

speaker: Leonard
text: Very impressive. And he's only fifteen years old.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Not bad. I myself started graduate school at fourteen.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Advantage, Kim.

speaker: Leonard
text: I thought maybe you boys could show Dennis around, let him see why we're the best physics research facility in the country.

speaker: Dennis
text: Well, I lost a year while my family was tunneling out of North Korea. I already know you're not. You don't have an open science grid computer or a real electron laser. And the string theory research being done there is nothing but a dead end.

text: Excuse me, that's my research and it is by no means a dead end.
